records.literal_gloss: And answered Job the LORD and said:

en.L: And Job answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said:

decisions.choice: Job's second answer to the LORD
decisions.reason: After the first speech Job answered briefly and said he would speak no more (40:3-5). Now, after the second speech (40:6-41:26), he answers again. As with the other speech introductions, these words are prose and the answer (42:2-6) is poetry.

decisions.choice: answered (B), said to (R), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs; Literal keeps both, and Balanced and Readable say it once, as in the other speech introductions of Job (40:3).

source.text: יָ֭דַעְתִּי כִּי־כֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וְלֹא־יִבָּצֵ֖ר מִמְּךָ֣ מְזִמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I know that everything you are able [to do], and not is withheld from you a purpose.

en.L: I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able [to do] everything, \q and no purpose is withheld from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do everything; \q no purpose of {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} can be stopped.
en.R: I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do anything. \q No one can stop {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} plans.

decisions.choice: I know (as read)
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell "you know"; the scribes' reading note, followed by the word data and by nearly all translations, gives "I know". Job is confessing what he has now learned.

decisions.choice: no purpose is withheld from you: nothing God plans is beyond his power
decisions.reason: The same verb and noun are used in Genesis 11:6, where the LORD says that nothing the builders of Babel plan will be withheld from them. What was a danger in human hands is simply true of God.

decisions.choice: purpose: God's plan
decisions.reason: The noun usually means a scheme or plot, often a bad one (21:27). Of God it is his considered purpose, the "counsel" of 38:2 and 42:3 that Job now sees he could not grasp.

source.text: מִ֤י זֶ֨ה׀מַעְלִ֥ים עֵצָ֗ה בְּֽלִ֫י דָ֥עַת לָכֵ֣ן הִ֭גַּדְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין נִפְלָא֥וֹת מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְלֹ֣א אֵדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] this hiding counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have declared and not I understood, [things] too wonderful for me, and not I knew.

en.L: Who [is] this who hides counsel without knowledge? \q Therefore I have spoken, and I did not understand, \q [things] too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
en.B: You asked, "Who is this who hides {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plan without knowledge?" \q Truly I have spoken of what I did not understand, \q things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
en.R: You asked, "Who is this who hides {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plans by talking without knowing?" \q It is true: I talked about things I did not understand, \q things too wonderful for me to know.

decisions.choice: Job quotes the LORD's first question (38:2)
decisions.reason: These are almost exactly the words with which the LORD began (38:2), with "hides" in place of "darkens". Job repeats the question and answers it: the one who spoke without knowledge was himself.

decisions.choice: therefore: so it is true, I spoke
decisions.reason: The word usually means "therefore". Here it draws the conclusion from the question: since that is what was said of him, Job admits it.

decisions.choice: too wonderful for me: beyond what I can understand
decisions.reason: The word describes what is beyond human reach or understanding (Psalm 131:1; Psalm 139:6). Job does not say he was wicked; he says he spoke of things beyond his understanding.

decisions.choice: You asked, "..." (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives no sign that Job is quoting. Balanced and Readable supply "You asked" and quotation marks so the reader does not take the question for Job's own (m1). As in 38:2, "counsel" is rendered "plan", and the pronoun refers to God.

records.literal_gloss: Hear, please, and I will speak; I will ask you, and you make known to me.

en.L: Hear, please, and I will speak; \q I will ask you, and you make [it] known to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: You said, "Listen now, and I will speak; \q I will question you, and you will answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: You said, "Listen, and I will speak. \q I will ask you questions, and you must answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: Job quotes the LORD's challenge (38:3; 40:7)
decisions.reason: The second line repeats the LORD's words in 38:3 and 40:7 exactly: "I will ask you, and you make it known to me." So the verse is best read as a second quotation, like 42:3. Some read it as Job asking God to listen to him, but the words are the LORD's.

decisions.choice: hear, and I will speak: the reverse of what Job once demanded
decisions.reason: Job had challenged God: "Call, and I will answer, or let me speak, and you reply" (13:22). In the storm it was God who called and Job who had to answer.

decisions.choice: You said, "..." (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 42:3, Balanced and Readable mark the quotation (m1). In the quoted words "I" is the LORD and "you" is Job.

records.literal_gloss: By hearing of ear I had heard of you, and now eye my has seen you.

en.L: By the hearing of the ear I had heard of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q but now my eye has seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: I had heard of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} by what my ears were told, \q but now my own eyes have seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Before, I had only heard about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q But now I have seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with my own eyes.

decisions.choice: by the hearing of the ear: by report, what others say
decisions.reason: To know by the hearing of the ear is to know secondhand, by what one has been told (28:22; Psalm 18:45). Job's knowledge of God had been real, but at a distance.

decisions.choice: now my eye has seen you: Job has met God himself
decisions.reason: Job had longed to see God (19:26-27). In the storm God has come and spoken to him. The text does not describe what Job saw; the point is that he has met God directly and not only heard about him.

decisions.choice: Before, I had only heard (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "before" and "only" to bring out the contrast between hearing and seeing (m1).

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I reject and I repent on dust and ashes.

en.L: Therefore I retract [my words], \q and I repent in dust and ashes.
en.B: So I take back what I said, \q and I repent in dust and ashes.
en.R: So I take back what I said. \q I am sorry, and I repent in dust and ashes.

decisions.choice: I reject: I retract what I said
decisions.reason: The verb means to reject or despise, but here it has no object, and what Job rejects must be supplied. Most likely it is his own words, spoken without knowledge (42:3; compare 40:4-5). Others supply "myself", or take it as in 7:16, "I loathe my life".

decisions.choice: I repent: I turn from my former position
alternatives: I am comforted concerning dust and ashes
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to be sorry and change one's mind, or to be comforted (2:11 uses it of the friends coming to comfort Job). With "concerning" it can mean "I relent concerning" or "I am comforted about dust and ashes", that is, Job accepts his place as a mortal man. Repentance is followed here, but the line is not certain.

decisions.choice: dust and ashes: the sign of mourning and of human lowliness
decisions.reason: Job had sat among the ashes (2:8), and his friends threw dust on their heads (2:12). Dust and ashes also stand for what a human being is before God (30:19; Genesis 18:27).

decisions.choice: what Job repents of: not the sins the friends charged him with
decisions.reason: The LORD says next that Job has spoken what is right about him, and the friends have not (42:7-8). Job does not confess the hidden wickedness the friends claimed caused his suffering; he takes back his demand that God answer to him, spoken without knowledge (42:3).

decisions.choice: [my words] (L); what I said (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for the verb. Every level supplies "my words" or "what I said" following m1; Literal brackets it.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל־אִיּ֑וֹב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־אֱלִיפַ֣ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֗י חָרָ֨ה אַפִּ֤י בְךָ֙ וּבִשְׁנֵ֣י רֵעֶ֔יךָ כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after had spoken the LORD the words the these to Job, and said the LORD to Eliphaz the Temanite: burns my anger against you and against two [of] your friends, for not you have spoken of me [what is] right like my slave Job.

en.L: And it happened, after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken these words to Job, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My anger burns against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [what is] right, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Job [has].
en.B: After {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken these words to Job, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My anger burns against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} what is right, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job has.
en.R: After {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} finished speaking to Job, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "I am angry with you and your two friends. You have not said what is right about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job has.

decisions.choice: the story returns to prose, and the LORD speaks to the friends
decisions.reason: With these words the book returns to the prose of chapters 1-2 and to the divine name used there. The LORD has finished speaking to Job (38:1-41:26) and now turns to Eliphaz, the first and probably the oldest of the friends (4:1; 15:10).

decisions.choice: what is right: what is true and well founded
decisions.reason: The word means firm, established, reliable (Psalm 5:10, "nothing reliable in their mouth"). The friends' speeches about God were not true to him; Job's were.

decisions.choice: of me: about God
decisions.reason: The preposition usually means "to", but it can also mean "about". The friends spoke about God rather than to him, while Job spoke to God as well as about him. "About me" fits both the friends and Job, and is followed; "to me" would point to Job's prayers and complaints addressed to God.

decisions.choice: Job, not the friends, spoke rightly
decisions.reason: The friends had defended God by insisting that Job must be guilty; Job had warned them that God would rebuke them for speaking falsely on his behalf (13:7-10). The LORD calls Job "my servant" as in the prologue (1:8; 2:3). He has rebuked Job's words spoken without knowledge (38:2; 40:2, 8), but he does not count Job among those who spoke wrongly of him.

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:8, Literal says "slave" and Balanced and Readable "servant" for the word that means one who belongs to his master; here it is a title of honor.

decisions.choice: I am angry with you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of burning anger means.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה קְחֽוּ־לָכֶ֣ם שִׁבְעָֽה־פָרִים֩ וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֵילִ֜ים וּלְכ֣וּ׀אֶל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֤ם עוֹלָה֙ בַּֽעַדְכֶ֔ם וְאִיּ֣וֹב עַבְדִּ֔י יִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֧י אִם־פָּנָ֣יו אֶשָּׂ֗א לְבִלְתִּ֞י עֲשׂ֤וֹת עִמָּכֶם֙ נְבָלָ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams and go to my slave Job, and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves, and Job my slave will pray for you; for his face I will lift up, so as not to do with you folly, for not you have spoken of me [what is] right like my slave Job.

en.L: And now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Job and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves, and Job {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave will pray for you; for his face I will lift up, so that I do not deal with you [according to your] folly; for you have not spoken of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [what is] right, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Job [has]."
en.B: So now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not deal with you as your folly deserves. For you have not spoken of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} what is right, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job has."
en.R: Now take seven bulls and seven rams. Go to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job and offer them as a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer. Then I will not punish you for your foolishness. You have not said what is right about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job has."

decisions.choice: seven bulls and seven rams as a burnt offering: a large and complete sacrifice
decisions.reason: Seven of each makes a full and costly offering (Numbers 23:1; 1 Chronicles 15:26). The burnt offering was wholly burned on the altar. Job had offered burnt offerings for his children in case they had sinned (1:5); now he stands between God and his friends.

decisions.choice: I will lift up his face: I will accept him and his prayer
decisions.reason: To lift up someone's face is to receive them with favor and grant their request (Genesis 19:21; 1 Samuel 25:35). God will hear Job's prayer for the friends who wronged him.

decisions.choice: not to deal with you according to your folly
alternatives: so as not to disgrace you
decisions.reason: The noun means senseless or shameful folly, the outrage a fool commits (Genesis 34:7; 1 Samuel 25:25). It can mean either the friends' folly, which God will not repay, or a disgrace God would bring on them; both mean that God will spare them because of Job's prayer.

decisions.choice: Job prays for the friends
decisions.reason: Job, whom the friends condemned, becomes the one through whose prayer they are forgiven, as Abraham and Moses prayed for others (Genesis 20:7, 17; Numbers 21:7).

decisions.choice: I will accept his prayer (B, R)
alternatives: I will lift up his face
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m2) and name the prayer it refers to.

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 42:7 and 1:8.

source.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ אֱלִיפַ֨ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֜י וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י צֹפַר֙ הַנַּ֣עֲמָתִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite, Zophar the Naamathite, and did as had spoken to them the LORD; and lifted up the LORD [the] face of Job.

en.L: And Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite [and] Zophar the Naamathite went and did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to them; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lifted up the face of Job.
en.B: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} accepted Job's prayer.
en.R: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} accepted Job's prayer.

decisions.choice: the LORD lifted up the face of Job: he accepted Job and his prayer
decisions.reason: The same idiom as in 42:8: God received Job with favor and granted his prayer for his friends. The friends are named in full for the last time, as when they came (2:11).

decisions.choice: accepted Job's prayer (B, R)
alternatives: lifted up the face of Job
decisions.reason: As in 42:8, Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom and name the prayer.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת־שְׁב֣וּת אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַ֧יֹּסֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the LORD turned back the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friends, and increased the LORD all that [belonged] to Job to double.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned back the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friends, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} increased all that Job had to double.
en.B: When Job prayed for his friends, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} restored his fortunes, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Job twice as much as he had before.
en.R: When Job prayed for his friends, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made him prosperous again. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave him twice as much as he had before.

decisions.choice: turned back the captivity: restored his fortunes
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of God bringing his people back from exile (Deuteronomy 30:3; Psalm 126:4) and more generally of restoring what was lost. Job was never a captive; the LORD turned his ruin back into prosperity. The written text and the scribes' reading note spell the noun slightly differently; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: when he prayed for his friends
decisions.reason: The restoration comes as Job prays for the men who had wronged him (42:8). The text links the two without saying that the one caused the other.

decisions.choice: to double: twice as much
decisions.reason: The numbers in 42:12 are exactly twice those of 1:3. Double repayment is what the law requires of a thief (Exodus 22:3, 6, 8, numbered 22:4, 7, 9 in many Bibles), so Job's losses are more than made good.

decisions.choice: restored his fortunes (B); made him prosperous again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the phrase (m1); Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל־אֶחָ֨יו וְכָל־אַחְיוֹתָ֜יו וְכָל־יֹדְעָ֣יו לְפָנִ֗ים וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ עִמּ֣וֹ לֶחֶם֮ בְּבֵיתוֹ֒ וַיָּנֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ וַיְנַחֲמ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עַ֚ל כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיִּתְּנוּ־ל֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ קְשִׂיטָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאִ֕ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם זָהָ֖ב אֶחָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came to him all his brothers and all his sisters and all [who] knew him before, and they ate with him bread in his house; and they showed sympathy to him and comforted him over all the evil that had brought the LORD on him; and gave to him each one qesitah one and each one ring of gold one.

en.L: And there came to him all his brothers and all his sisters and all who had known him before, and they ate bread with him in his house; and they showed him sympathy and comforted him over all the evil that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought upon him; and each gave him one qesitah and each one ring of gold.
en.B: All his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate a meal with him in his house. They showed him sympathy and comforted him for all the trouble {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought on him, and each of them gave him {{units:a piece of money|a qesitah}} and a gold ring.
en.R: All his brothers and sisters and all his old friends came to his house and ate with him. They showed that they cared, and they comforted him for all the trouble {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought on him. Each of them gave him {{units:a piece of money|a qesitah}} and a gold ring.

decisions.choice: the evil: the disaster, the trouble
decisions.reason: The word means harm or disaster as well as wickedness. It is the "evil" Job accepted from God in 2:10 and the "evil" the friends heard had come on him in 2:11; it is suffering, not sin.

decisions.choice: that the LORD had brought on him
decisions.reason: The narrator says what Job himself said (1:21; 2:10): the trouble came from the LORD. The Accuser of chapters 1-2 is not mentioned again; Job is never told of him.

decisions.choice: showed him sympathy and comforted him
decisions.reason: The same two verbs describe the friends' visit in 2:11. Now Job's family and old acquaintances, who had kept away from him (19:13-14), come and do what the friends set out to do.

decisions.choice: qesitah: a piece of money of unknown value
decisions.reason: The word is found elsewhere only in Genesis 33:19 and Joshua 24:32, where Jacob buys land for a hundred of them. It was probably a weight of silver; its value is not known.

decisions.choice: a piece of money, with "a qesitah" as the units setting (B, R)
decisions.reason: Since the value is unknown, Balanced and Readable describe it as a piece of money; the units setting gives the Hebrew name, which Literal keeps.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה בֵּרַ֛ךְ אֶת־אַחֲרִ֥ית אִיּ֖וֹב מֵרֵאשִׁת֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי־ל֡וֹ אַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר אֶ֜לֶף צֹ֗אן וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ גְּמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶֽלֶף־צֶ֥מֶד בָּקָ֖ר וְאֶ֥לֶף אֲתוֹנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning; and there were to him fourteen thousand sheep and six thousand camels and a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning; and he had 14,000 sheep and 6,000 camels and 1,000 yoke of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the last part of Job's life more than the first. He had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} blessed Job even more in the last part of his life than in the first. He now had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

decisions.choice: blessed: real blessing
decisions.reason: Here the verb means to bless, not the "curse" it stands for in 1:5, 11 and 2:5, 9 (see the decision at 1:5). As in 1:21, it is true blessing.

decisions.choice: his latter end more than his beginning
decisions.reason: Bildad had told Job that if he were pure, "your beginning will seem small, and your latter end will grow very great" (8:7). The words come true, though not for Bildad's reasons.

decisions.choice: the numbers are double those of 1:3
decisions.reason: In 1:3 Job had 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen and 500 female donkeys. Each number is now doubled (42:10).

decisions.choice: pairs of oxen (R)
decisions.reason: A yoke of oxen is a pair harnessed together for plowing; Readable says "pairs".

records.literal_gloss: And there were to him seven sons and three daughters.

en.L: And he had seven sons and three daughters.
en.B: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
en.R: He also had seven sons and three daughters.

decisions.choice: seven
decisions.reason: The word for seven has an unusual ending here, and some take it to mean "twice seven", so that Job's sons were doubled like his flocks. But the plain sense is seven, and Job's three daughters are not doubled; the sons, like the daughters, are as many as in 1:2, while the flocks and herds are doubled (42:12).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־הָֽאַחַת֙ יְמִימָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית קְצִיעָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית קֶ֥רֶן הַפּֽוּךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he called the name of the first Jemimah, and the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-happuch.

en.L: And he called the name of the first Jemimah, and the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-happuch.
en.B: He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
en.R: He named the first daughter Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.

decisions.choice: the meaning of the daughters' names
decisions.reason: Jemimah probably means "dove"; Keziah is cassia, a fragrant spice (Psalm 45:9); Keren-happuch means "horn of eye paint", a container for the dark cosmetic women used around their eyes (2 Kings 9:30). All three names speak of beauty, as the next verse does.

decisions.choice: the daughters are named, the sons are not
decisions.reason: Hebrew stories usually name sons and leave daughters unnamed. Here only the daughters are named, which gives them special honor (42:15).

source.text: וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א נָשִׁ֥ים יָפ֛וֹת כִּבְנ֥וֹת אִיּ֖וֹב בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם אֲבִיהֶ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And not were found women beautiful like [the] daughters of Job in all the land; and gave to them their father an inheritance among their brothers.

en.L: And there were not found women [as] beautiful as the daughters of Job in all the land; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
en.B: In all the land there were no women as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.
en.R: There were no women in the whole land as beautiful as Job's daughters. Their father gave them a share of his property, just as he did for their brothers.

decisions.choice: an inheritance among their brothers: the daughters inherit with the sons
decisions.reason: In Israel's law daughters inherited their father's land only when there were no sons (Numbers 27:1-11). Job gives his daughters a share alongside their brothers, a sign of his wealth and of his love for them.

decisions.choice: a share of his property (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the inheritance was.

source.text: וַיְחִ֤י אִיּוֹב֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־זֹ֔את מֵאָ֥ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיִּרְאֶ֗ה אֶת־בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֣י בָנָ֔יו אַרְבָּעָ֖ה דֹּרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lived Job after this a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons and [the] sons of his sons, four generations.

en.L: And Job lived after this 140 years, and saw his {{gender:children|sons}} and his {{gender:children's children|sons' sons}}, four generations.
en.B: After this Job lived 140 years, and he saw his {{gender:children and grandchildren|sons and grandsons}} to the fourth generation.
en.R: After this, Job lived 140 more years. He lived to see his {{gender:children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren|sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons}}, and their children too: four generations.

decisions.choice: seeing four generations: the blessing of a long life
decisions.reason: To live to see one's grandchildren and their children was a mark of God's blessing (Genesis 50:23; Psalm 128:6; Proverbs 17:6). Eliphaz had promised Job many descendants if he accepted God's correction (5:25).

decisions.choice: his sons: his children, daughters as well as sons
decisions.reason: The word means sons, but in a phrase like "his sons and his sons' sons" it means descendants of both sexes, and Job's daughters have just been named (42:14-15).

decisions.choice: and he saw (as read)
decisions.reason: The written text and the scribes' reading note spell the verb slightly differently; both mean "and he saw".

decisions.choice: children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, and their children too (R)
alternatives: his sons and his sons' sons, four generations
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the four generations.

records.literal_gloss: And died Job, old and full of days.

en.L: And Job died, old and full of days.
en.B: And Job died, old and satisfied with his days.
en.R: Then Job died. He was very old and had lived a long, full life.

decisions.choice: old and full of days: having lived a long and complete life
decisions.reason: The same words are said of Abraham (Genesis 25:8), Isaac (Genesis 35:29) and David (1 Chronicles 29:28). The word "full" means satisfied: Job dies having had all the life he could wish, like the great men of old.

decisions.choice: satisfied with his days (B); had lived a long, full life (R)
decisions.reason: "Full" is the word for being satisfied with food; Balanced brings out that sense, and Readable says what the phrase means (m1).
